probe.format_note: Single 9:16 film, 720x1280, 29.97 fps, 32.75 s (matches our default vertical format, no re-composition needed). Audio: AAC HE-AACv2 stereo 44.1 kHz, continuous (no silence below -40 dB for 0.3 s or longer), mean -20.9 dB, peak -2.1 dB; the on-screen caption changes phrase by phrase like a narrated script, so read as narration over a music bed (not listened to, not analysed for beats); third-party audio, never reused.

rights_note: found by the owner on Pinterest with a style search (file «infographic motion design.mp4»), given by the owner via Downloads/refrencee on 2026-11-03; origin not stated → plan mode ADAPT, never RECREATE

mode.why: third-party motivational trading reel of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and the soft blue 3D look only, never its shots one by one, its copy, its numbers, its calendar years, its characters as designed or its CTA (owner note); a voiceover package defaults to REEL

ignored.why: all English copy (the trading-discipline script: 'Extreme discipline' vs 'Casual Trying', 'Most traders spend years repeating the same mistakes', 'Same Habits / Same Emotions / same lack of structure', 'Everything Changes', 'A single focused year can rewrite your future') is third-party copy; never reused, translated or paraphrased as our line

the chart values and labels ('40.256', 'Exercitation Ullamco' placeholder text, '58 % Growth', '35 % incline', axis 10/20) are placeholder or third-party numbers; any number on our screen comes only from the content package (data-viz.md)

the desk calendar flipping 2018 to 2025 is the creator's prop for its own line; only the technique (a counter object flips its pages to show time passing) may be used, and only if our voice-over talks about time
'income stats', 'Invested', 'Withdrawn' and the rising curve are the creator's trading chart; our charts carry only package data

the glossy round-headed characters, the white desk with monitor, the 'Task 1-4' checklist and the 'Share this post' end card with a paper plane are the creator's scenes and CTA; we draw our own subjects from the voice-over in this rendering style, and our ending is the brand logo outro and our own CTA
the audio track (narration and music) is third-party; L2 uses our voice-over and L6 builds our sound

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 at 360 px wide (6 sheets, 4x3, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found 5 cuts: 5.11, 12.25, 17.65, 21.19, 22.56 s; two more scene changes (about 8.3 s calendar to cards, about 24.9 s checklist to '1 YEAR') and the whip at about 26.3 s were found by eye on the 2 fps sheets; dense sheets at fps=10 around 4.6-5.8, 11.7-12.9, 16.9-18.1, 25.6-26.8, 28.4-29.6 s and fps=5 around 20.6-23.0 s (6 dense sheets, all viewed). Spans accurate to about ±0.1 s at detected cuts and ±0.25 s at changes found by eye. silencedetect + volumedetect on the audio. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

visual_language: A soft-3D infographic narrative reel: ten scenes, each a single bold visual metaphor for one line of narration, all on one airy blue world. Medium: code-built 3D (charts standing in space, a glossy prop object, glossy cards, a planet-like sphere with liquid, simple primitive characters, a desk scene) mixed with large typography. Typography runs on two layers: a constant small caption line (regular geometric sans, dark navy on light scenes and white on dark ones, cap height about 1.5% of frame height, centred at about 19% of height) that changes phrase by phrase with the narration, and one hero type element per scene (bold geometric sans labels, white text on glossy cards, ultra-condensed heavy headlines for turning points like the 'changes' word, '1 YEAR' wall and end card). Rhythm: average shot about 3.3 s, caption phrases change every 0.8-1.5 s, cuts land on phrase boundaries; whip pans with motion blur carry three transitions, one cross-dissolve, one iris, the rest hard or soft cuts. Easing is smooth and slow for camera and liquid, snappy for flips and ticks. Palette: a white hotspot in the upper left falling into periwinkle and electric blue, deep navy type, glossy navy-black and violet objects, and one dark scene pair (near-black with blue rim light) for the turning point. Signature moments: the camera riding a chart line; pages flipping off a time counter; cards sliding in and stacking; the liquid drop that pierces the dark sphere and becomes a glowing pearl over the 'changes' headline; the iris onto a ticking checklist; a small figure in front of a giant word wall; the word-by-word peak line.
look: Real soft 3D (studio CG style), not flat: objects have volume, perspective and glossy materials. Light and shadow: a big soft key light from the upper left that blows out to a white hotspot, blue ambient fill, rim lights on dark objects, soft reflections on a glossy floor, no hard shadows. Materials: glossy black and navy plastic with blue gradient sheen (calendar, cards), thick glossy liquid (the drop), dark matte sphere with a pale rim highlight, glass spheres with fresnel rim and inner glow (end-card character), clean white matte desk. Depth of field: strong lens blur by depth on charts, card stacks, lists and foreground type. Background: a smooth blurred white-to-periwinkle-to-electric-blue gradient studio sky, sometimes with a white floor and horizon; twice it goes to near-black navy with blue rim light for the dark turning point.
code_translation: Built as real 3D in code with three.js: a gradient sky shader (white hotspot upper left, periwinkle, electric-blue glow on the right) mapped onto the brand background and accent roles; MeshPhysicalMaterial with clearcoat for glossy objects, a soft key light from the upper left, blue hemisphere fill, rim lights for dark scenes; depth of field as a bokeh post-pass or per-layer CSS blur by depth; whip pans as a fast camera yaw plus a directional motion-blur pass, cut on the blur; iris as a growing circular mask with a glowing rim. Charts are lines drawn by stroke-dashoffset on perspective planes; cards are rounded planes with gradient clearcoat; the liquid stem is an animated tube or SVG path with gradient fill and a bloom on the pearl. Type: the caption line and all hero type are HTML or texture overlays in the brand Persian font, whole words only, never split letters (rtl-grammar.md); the caption is centred, so it mirrors cleanly for Persian; letter-by-letter builds become word-by-word builds. Ultra-condensed headlines use the brand's heaviest display weight, never a substitute font. Subjects and props come from our voice-over, never the reference's.
continuity: One world: the same soft blue gradient studio sky and white hotspot light every scene, so cuts feel like moves inside one place.
Constant caption line: a small phrase line at the same height in every scene changes with the narration, while the hero element below carries the metaphor.
Camera rides the data: the camera travels along a growing line on a chart standing in space, then pulls back to reveal a comparison.
Whip pan with motion blur: the scene smears sideways or vertically and the cut is hidden inside the blur; the next scene can enter still moving in the same direction.
Pages flip off a counter: a time-counter object flips page by page and each page tumbles off to the side.
Stacking cards: one glossy card slides in per voiced item, the stack grows down the frame, then the camera orbits it in depth.
Pierce and invert: a slow element descends, pierces a surface, and the light flips from bright sky to dark depth, landing the turning-point headline in the dark.
Cross-dissolve to dark: a bright scene dissolves into a near-black rim-lit scene and the caption flips from navy to white.
Iris reveal: a glowing circle opens from the centre of a dark scene onto the next bright scene.
Tick on the word: list rows in steep perspective get a tick each as the voice names them, depth of field leading down the list.
Subject before a giant word: a small 3D subject stands in front of a giant word that rises behind it like a wall.
Word alone on the empty world: the peak line is given one word at a time on the bare gradient, each word darkening into place.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its English script, its numbers and placeholder text, the calendar years, the 'Task' list, its characters as designed, the 'Share this post' end card, its audio, or its scene order one by one.

The caption line is tiny (cap height about 1.5% of frame height, about 19 px at 1280): in our film it must meet the minimum text size and hold times (safe-zones.md), so it is set larger than the reference.

Persian runs right to left: the centred caption mirrors cleanly, but chart lines rising left to right, cards sliding in from the right, whip-pan directions and letter-by-letter builds are mirrored or made word by word for Persian (rtl-grammar.md).
Ultra-condensed heavy display type is central to the turning points: use the brand's heaviest Persian weight at large size; never fake condensing by scaling the font horizontally.
The look is real soft 3D with glossy materials, lens blur and motion blur: built in three.js (D55), never flattened into 2D shapes; render time is higher than a flat film.
Third-party charts show unsourced numbers: our charts use only numbers from the package with sources (data-viz.md); a decorative curve carries no values.
The palette is white, periwinkle and electric blue with navy type: mapped onto brand colour roles, never the literal blue if the brand differs; colours read by eye, not sampled.
Two scene changes (about 8.3 s and 24.9 s) and the whip at about 26.3 s were found by eye (±0.25 s); our film's scene changes are placed on voice timing, not on these spans.
The film ends on a 'share' CTA with the creator's characters: our film ends on our CTA and the brand logo outro.
Audio is third-party narration and music; ignored, L2 and L6 build ours.
